topics.title: Equation of a Straight Line
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Understand the relationship between a linear equation y=mx+c and its graph. (k, u)
Determine the x and y intercepts of a given linear graph. (u, s)
Determine the gradient of a straight line. (u, s)
State the gradient of a straight line when given the equation. (k, u)
Apply the relationship of gradients of parallel and perpendicular lines to determine the equation of a straight line. (k, u, s)

body.text: Building on Senior 1's y = mx + c, the y-intercept is where the line crosses the y-axis (x = 0, so y = c), and the x-intercept is where it crosses the x-axis (y = 0). For y = 2x - 6: the y-intercept is (0, -6); setting y = 0 gives 0 = 2x - 6, so x = 3, giving x-intercept (3, 0).

Parallel lines always have equal gradients. Perpendicular lines have gradients that multiply to give -1 — if one line has gradient m, a line perpendicular to it has gradient -1/m. A line with gradient 2 is perpendicular to a line with gradient -1/2, since 2 x (-1/2) = -1.

Find the equation of the line through (1, 5) that is parallel to y = 3x + 2. Parallel means the same gradient, m = 3. Using y = mx + c with the point (1, 5): 5 = 3(1) + c, so c = 2. The line is y = 3x + 2 — the same line, since (1,5) already lies on it. Trying (1, 8) instead: 8 = 3(1) + c gives c = 5, so the equation is y = 3x + 5.
